Subject: Tri-Zone Dedicated Sizing for Sable Analytics (deal-linked request)

Hi Megan / Sable team —

Great to speak last week. As we scope the Dedicated capacity commitment tied to RDW-2027-0891, you asked for a tri-zone (US/EU/APAC) plan that guarantees regional isolation and predictable throughput during launch and steady state. To get alignment, can you confirm the traffic and SLO assumptions below so we can produce a costed SKU/commitment proposal: 

- Expected steady QPS (text gen requests) by region for first 6 months
- Peak concurrent sessions and 99th pct latency target per region
- Preferred model variants (e.g., redwood-gpt-xl-quant/float) and whether you require float FP16 in EU for compliance
- Data residency / VPC peering windows and expected daily offload batch jobs (embedding generation)

I’ve looped in Karthik and Marcus to draft a capacity sketch and an initial SKU estimate. If you can attach the traffic sample (CSV) and any procurement timeline (PO target date), we’ll aim to return a recommended pool sizing and tranche schedule by end of day Thursday.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Laura —

Quick pass on assumptions we should bake into the sketch:

- Baseline concurrency per request type: 60% text-gen, 30% embedding batch, 10% rerank. Use 95th percentile token length = 150 for text-gen costing.
- Start with reservation units mapped to GPU types: 8x A100-80GB equiv per 10k steady QPS for gen (ballpark); embeddings use pooled smaller instances (e.g., 4xA10 equivalents per 5k monthly embedding units)
- Regional buffer: +25% headroom in APAC for launch month; +15% in EU; +10% in US
- Canary / can-autoscale buffer: keep 2 reserved nodes per zone for failover (charged as reserved)

I’ll spin up an initial SKU estimate workbook (sable-tri-zone-sku-estimate.xlsx) with three tranches: pilot (30 days), ramp (3 months), steady (12 months). I’ll include cost deltas for quantized vs. FP16 model paths. Expect draft by 16 Sep EOD.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect

Megan —

Appreciate the traffic profile — that made estimates straightforward. Attached is the SKU workbook (sable-tri-zone-sku-estimate.xlsx) and a short mutual action plan draft. Highlights: 

- Pilot tranche (30 days): US: reserve 40 vGPU-equivalents (mapped to 5xA100-80GB), EU: 14 vGPU-eq (2xA100 + 2xA10 mix), APAC: 8 vGPU-eq (A10-class). This covers steady + expected initial bursts with our recommended +headroom.
- Ramp tranche (months 2–4): scale US to 60 vGPU-eq, EU to 24, APAC to 12 — triggered by utilization thresholds and the agreed weekly usage reports.
- Steady tranche (12 months): US 50 vGPU-eq, EU 20, APAC 10 with autoscale burst lanes brokered by Redwood Dedicated (burst billing applies).
- Cost delta: quantized path reduces compute unit cost ~32% vs FP16 for gen; we show both lanes per region in worksheet.
- SLA/regional isolation: we propose VPC peering + dedicated control plane for EU workloads; SLA appendix included in MAP.

Tranche = phased reserved commitment. Billing: reserved capacity is invoiced monthly against the committed tranche; spike/overage handled via burst lanes at agreed rates. The SKU workbook includes both invoice examples and a sample PO line item you can copy into procurement.

Next steps: 1) Megan/legal confirm EU isolation language and PO cadence, 2) Karthik/Marcus will produce a short ops runbook for on-call handover during the pilot, 3) we schedule a 30-minute kickoff with SRE and your ops next Tue.

Thanks — sending attachment now.

Laura
Senior Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
